card.title: Cover Story Logistics
card.instruction: Accept that a secret plan exists, then focus on schedules, witnesses, explanations, cleanup, and what everyone must remember.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For Dad's surprise picnic, where can forty guests board the bus unseen?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Outside my shop. Dad never goes there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Tell everyone to arrive separately so the neighbours don't mention a crowd.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Dad's offered to open the shop for me while I organise it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then board at the library. Ring all forty guests; no group message Dad might see. Who's collecting him after we leave?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 treats unseen boarding as logistics, A3 manages neighbor witnesses, and A5 changes venue and contact method when Dad will be present.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's shop location informs A3's staggered arrivals; B4's Dad-opening update causes A5's library move and individual calls.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers a sensible venue and B4 discloses a new conflict that actually invalidates it.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's witness problem to alter the plan and check the remaining task of collecting Dad.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes forty guests, a bus and Dad's surprise picnic before any concealment procedure is proposed.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's no-group-message and collection question develop B4's specific risk rather than adding a joke.

coach2.inferred: A1-B4 establish family picnic organizers keeping the recipient unaware.

coach2.firstDefect: No mandatory defect; A accepts the secret plan and concretely manages its moving logistical parts.
